- When sentiment is high (≥0.6) and forecast shows strong upward bias, reduce peak forecasts by 5–10% to avoid overreaction.  
- If sentiment is low (≤0.3) and forecast is overly conservative, slightly increase early-period forecasts to capture mean reversion.  
- After a sharp price spike, model tends to overshoot — cap 3–5 day forecasts at 10–15% below the peak to avoid overcorrection.  
- In low-sentiment periods, model underestimates downside risk — add 2–3% buffer to forecasted lows to account for volatility.  
- Forecast horizon >14 days shows persistent lag — adjust by adding 1–2% per day to catch upward momentum.  
- When sentiment is rising (e.g., 0.7–0.9) and price is flat, model often underestimates breakout — increase forecast slope by 0.5–1.0% per day.
